citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not perform complete daily observation of all animals to assess their health and well-being. Two veterinary
medical officers observed two animals in need of veterinary care:
** A juvenile russian dwarf hamster housed indoors with approximately 19 other hamsters was identified with crusting
scabs on the front forelimbs. The scab on the right forelimb was observed along his forelimb between the elbow and wrist.
The right arm was mildly swollen.
** A juvenile budgerigar housed with another parakeet was observed resting on a perch. An accumulation of feces was
visible under the bird and the rest of the perch was clean, indicating that the bird had spent the majority of its time in that
area. When the inspector approached the bird, he adjusted his stance and appeared uncomfortable on the left foot. When
removed from the enclosure for closer inspection, the left foot had mild redness, skin flaking on the foot and hock area,
and mild swelling on the toe.
The facility had not identified these conditions prior to the inspection. This has prevented the attending veterinarian from
the opportunity to provide timely medical care for the animals.
The facility initiated veterinary treatment at the time of inspection. Continue to correct by ensuring that daily observation of
all animals is performed to assess their health and well-being.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Scott Welch, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
